perf.summary: The inner while loop computes run % period for every character compared, a division on the hottest path.
perf.currentCost: Per comparison: an integer modulo (run % period), ~20-40 cycles on many mobile cores, plus an add for i+(run%period). This runs O(n) times per (period,i) pair.
perf.proposedChange: Maintain a rolling index m that tracks run % period without division: start m = 0; compare s[i+run] == s[i+m]; after each step do run++ and m++ then if (m == period) m = 0;. This replaces the modulo with an increment and a single compare/branch (or branchless: m = (m + 1 == period ? 0 : m + 1)).
perf.rationale: Replaces a div by an add+compare, eliminating the longest-latency op in the inner loop; the compare is well-predicted (taken once per period), and s[i+m] base offset is now incremental.
perf.risk: Rolling counter must reset to 0 exactly when it reaches period, reproducing run % period for all run >= 0. Result identical.

perf.summary: AggressiveInlining is applied to a large doubly-nested-loop method where inlining cannot help and may hurt.
perf.currentCost: The attribute forces the JIT/Burst to consider inlining a big function body into every caller, bloating call sites and instruction cache with no benefit since the cost is inside the loops, not the call.
perf.proposedChange: Remove [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)] from Find. Reserve AggressiveInlining for the small leaf helpers (GetNext/SetNext style), not loop-bearing entry points.
perf.rationale: Inlining a hot leaf saves a call; inlining a multi-loop driver only grows code size and I-cache pressure. Removing it lets the optimizer keep the loop body tight and out-of-line.
perf.risk: None functionally; this is a codegen hint only. Same output.

perf.summary: Loop bound period * 2 <= n recomputes the multiply each outer iteration and the inner bound n - 2*period each entry.
perf.currentCost: A multiply (period*2) in the outer condition and 2*period recomputed for the inner loop bound; minor but per outer iteration.
perf.proposedChange: Hoist int twoP = period << 1; reuse in both the outer guard (twoP <= n) and inner bound (i <= n - twoP). Strength-reduce *2 to <<1.
perf.rationale: Removes a redundant multiply and reuses a single shifted value; trivial but free and clarifies intent.
perf.risk: period is positive so <<1 == *2 exactly. No change in behavior.
